units.summary: statusRecorder gains an optional onStatus callback invoked when the final status is written. It is the hook that lets the breaker learn the outcome before the body finishes.
units.headline: statusRecorder gets onStatus callback for status-time reporting
units.reason: Adds a struct field that drives breaker accounting timing for every proxied request.
focus: onStatus is only set in serveThroughBreaker; other users of statusRecorder see nil and are unaffected

units.summary: WriteHeader now calls onStatus with the final status (>=200 or 101) before forwarding the header. The callback runs synchronously inside the response write path.
units.headline: WriteHeader now reports final status to breaker callback
units.reason: Changes when circuit-breaker outcomes are recorded, on the hot response path.
focus: callback runs before the header reaches the client; confirm it cannot block or panic
1xx informational codes other than 101 correctly do not report
repeated WriteHeader calls only report once via sync.Once

units.summary: Introduces groupBreaker as an alias for gobreaker's two-step circuit breaker so outcomes can be reported separately from the call.
units.headline: Add groupBreaker alias for the two-step circuit breaker
units.reason: A type alias only; the behavioral change is in newGroupBreaker and serveThroughBreaker.

units.summary: newGroupBreaker now constructs a TwoStepCircuitBreaker with the same settings. This changes the API callers use to record outcomes.
units.headline: newGroupBreaker builds a two-step breaker instead of a one-shot
units.reason: Changes the breaker implementation used for all groups; semantics depend on callers reporting every outcome.
focus: every Allow() caller must call done exactly once, or the half-open slot leaks
the same Settings (IsExcluded, ReadyToTrip) still apply under two-step

units.summary: The request is no longer run inside cb.Execute. It uses Allow() and reports the outcome when the response status is written, or on return or panic, guarded by sync.Once. This stops a long watch from holding a half-open breaker's trial slot.
units.headline: Breaker outcome reported at status write, not handler return
units.reason: Rewrites breaker accounting, panic handling and ordering of the open-state 503 path.
focus: a handler that writes the body without calling WriteHeader is still reported on return
the panic path reports once and re-panics, including http.ErrAbortHandler
status 5xx at header time is counted as a failure, and caller-gone is still excluded
Execute used to recover and re-panic; confirm equivalent state handling

units.summary: Test helper parameter type changed to the groupBreaker alias to match production.
units.headline: Test helper takes groupBreaker type
units.reason: Test-only type signature update to match the new breaker type.

units.summary: Test now builds a two-step breaker so it matches the production type. The assertions are unchanged.
units.headline: Half-open cap test uses two-step breaker
units.reason: Test-only constructor swap, with no assertions removed or changed.

units.summary: Test helper trips the breaker through Allow() and done(err) instead of Execute. This is the equivalent forced failure for a two-step breaker.
units.headline: tripBreaker uses Allow/done to force a failure
units.reason: Test-only helper adapted to the new breaker API with equivalent effect.
